how: Each concept was asked three ways: A in numbers only, B as a Hindi story, C as a Bhili story (children who speak Hindi at home skip C). Which ones a child got right puts them in a group. Tap a group to see who is in it and what to do. "Seen once" means a quick re-check confirms the group.

about.language_gap: Right in numbers (A) and in the Bhili story (C), wrong in the Hindi story (B). They can do the maths; the Hindi words are what stop them.
about.word_problem_gap: Right in numbers (A), wrong in the stories (B and C). They can do the sum, but can't yet turn a story into one.
about.symbol_gap: Wrong in numbers (A), right in the stories (B and C). They can solve the story, but not yet read the written sum.
about.language_symbol_gap: Wrong in numbers (A) and the Hindi story (B), right in the Bhili story (C). They follow the maths in Bhili, but not yet in Hindi words or written symbols.
about.never_taught: Wrong in all three, and absent on every day this concept was taught. The lesson was missed, not failed.
about.taught_not_learned: Wrong in all three, though present when it was taught. The step-down probe finds the earlier concept to restart from.
about.clip_failed: Right in numbers (A) and the Hindi story (B), wrong in the Bhili story (C). Either they follow Hindi better than Bhili, or the Bhili clip is unclear.
about.inconsistent: Right in the Hindi story (B) only. This fits no learning pattern, so it may be a guess or a copied answer.
about.unclear: A box was blank, or held a number copied from the question. Not enough to tell.
about.not_checked: Absent on the check day, but present when this was taught.
about.ready: Right in all three. Ready for the next concept.
